newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov says grip on UES may be tightened.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov says grip on UES may be tightened.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Tuesday that the government could increase control over the vast national power utility Unified Energy System (UES).
"Government control may be increased, as the company is a natural monopoly from the point of view of energy and transport," he told a news conference.
Nemtsov has been put in charge of reforming Russia's natural monopolies -- the term used to describe state-controlled networks such as electricity, gas and railways.
Nemtsov also said that the Central Dispatching Unit, which controls the movement of power on the national grid which UES owns, would remain part of the company.

Speaking after a government meeting on reforming UES, he said that cabinet representatives on the board of directors of UES, of which Russia has about 52 percent, would meet separately in order to present a unified position to the company.
The presidency and chairmanship of the company, both currently held by Anatoly Dyakov, are to be split, he added.
Nemtsov said closed-doors meetings to award contracts, including to foreigners, had to be stopped, investor rights respected and an independent auditor appointed.

UES, which is Russia's largest company by sales and staff and one of its biggest by market capitalisation, controls the national power grid and wholesale market, has majority stakes in most local power utilities and owns generating plants.
Nemtsov said UES intended to cut tariffs to manufacturing industry by 13 percent this year. He was quoting Dyakov, who earlier addressed the meeting on restructuring UES.
Nemtsov also said regional power utilities should raise capital by issuing new shares to fund restructuring. He said the companies needed a way to attract investment funds.
"I mean increasing authorised capital of the regional companies," he said. "It needs to be done quickly."
